quarterly_data.quarter: Panasonic Holdings semi-annual report: H1 FY2026 (11-07-2025)
quarterly_data.signal: First half (April-September 2025, IFRS): net sales JPY 3,820,476 million (-10% YoY), operating profit JPY 164,996 million (-24%), profit before income taxes JPY 177.9 billion (-29%), net profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 142,404 million (-25%). Management states Connect, Industry and Energy grew but the deconsolidation of the Automotive business cut sales; profit fell on higher fixed costs from inflation, lower Energy profit as the automotive battery business worsened, and the Automotive deconsolidation. Segment sales / segment profit (then four reportable segments plus Other): Lifestyle JPY 1,692,976 million (-2%) / JPY 63,627 million (+28%); Connect JPY 629,992 million (+3%) / JPY 28,865 million (+18%); Industry JPY 573,531 million (+5%) / JPY 46,331 million (+50%); Energy JPY 446,895 million (+4%) / JPY 33,083 million (-39%); Other JPY 815,177 million (+1%) / JPY 22,805 million (-39%). Group capex JPY 307.5 billion (-15%), R&D expense JPY 208.2 billion (-18%). In May, Blue Yonder (a Panasonic Connect subsidiary) announced its cognitive solutions, a suite of planning SaaS with generative-AI-based agents
quarterly_data.figure: H1 net sales JPY 3,820,476 million (-10%); operating profit JPY 164,996 million (-24%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Panasonic Holdings semi-annual report: H1 FY2026 (11-07-2025)
quarterly_data.signal: Industry segment (first half to September 2025): management states sales rose 5% on growing demand for information and communications products such as capacitors and multilayer circuit board materials for generative-AI servers, and profit rose 50% on higher sales plus price revisions and rationalization. Sales by product: electronic devices JPY 292,449 million (prior-year half JPY 276,717 million), FA solutions JPY 48,876 million (JPY 43,223 million), electronic materials JPY 97,728 million (JPY 85,090 million)

players.product: BBU backup battery units, energy storage systems (ESS) and supercapacitors for AI data centers

quarterly_data.quarter: Panasonic Holdings semi-annual report: H1 FY2026 (11-07-2025)
quarterly_data.signal: Energy segment (first half to September 2025): management states industrial/consumer sales rose with strong energy storage systems for data centers, while automotive batteries declined as lower sales from Japanese plants and price revisions reflecting lower raw-material prices offset higher North American volumes; profit fell 39% as data-center storage gains were outweighed by US tariffs, start-up costs at the Kansas and Wakayama plants and lower domestic sales. Sales by product: industrial/consumer JPY 240,687 million (prior-year half JPY 192,094 million), automotive JPY 203,417 million (JPY 244,978 million). Panasonic Energy started mass production in July 2025 at its Kansas automotive battery plant, which aims for annual production capacity of about 32 GWh in the future
quarterly_data.figure: H1 industrial/consumer sales JPY 240,687 million (prior-year half JPY 192,094 million); Kansas plant mass production from July 2025, ~32 GWh target
